{{short description|German mathematician (born 1977)}}
'''Mathias Schacht''' (born 1977) is a German mathematician who specializes in [[graph theory]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/home/schacht/cv.html.en|title=Curriculum vitae: Mathias Schacht|accessdate=2015-09-30}}.</ref>

Schacht earned a diploma in business mathematics in 1999 from [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref name="cv"/> He did his graduate studies at [[Emory University]], completing a PhD in 2004 under the supervision of [[Vojtěch Rödl]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=89286}}</ref> His dissertation, on [[hypergraph]] generalizations of the [[Szemerédi regularity lemma]], won the 2006 Richard Rado Prize of the [[German Mathematical Society]].<ref name="cv"/> He worked at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] as a postdoctoral researcher and acting professor from 2004 until 2009, when he moved to the [[University of Hamburg]]. He received his [[habilitation]] from Humboldt University in 2010, and has been Heisenberg Professor at the University of Hamburg from 2010 to 2015.<ref name="cv"/>

In 2012, Schacht and Rödl won the [[George Pólya Prize]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] for their research on hypergraph regularity.<ref>{{citation|url=http://connect.siam.org/vojtech-rodl-and-mathias-schacht-honored-by-siam-with-george-polya-prize/|title=Vojtech Rodl and Mathias Schacht honored by SIAM with George Polya Prize|date=August 14, 2012|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|accessdate=2015-09-30}}.</ref>
